settings.tagline: The GraphQL-first headless CMS in a single Rust binary
settings.description: Tess is a self-hostable, GraphQL-first headless CMS written in Rust. Define content models at runtime, publish with review workflows, and run it on Docker, a VM or AWS Lambda.
settings.footerText: © 2026 Tess Dev Team. Community edition for personal use, Enterprise edition for commercial use.

data.title: Features
data.description: Content models at runtime, generated GraphQL API, review workflows, roles, six database backends, media, search, WebAssembly plugins and AWS Lambda support.

page.title: Features
page.description: Content models at runtime, generated GraphQL API, review workflows, roles, six database backends, media, search, WebAssembly plugins and AWS Lambda support.

sections.title: One binary, the whole content platform
sections.subtitle: Tess bundles the API, the admin UI and the business rules. Pick your database, your media store and your hosting.

sections.title: Field types
sections.body: `TEXT` (length bounds, regex format), `MARKDOWN` (raw HTML refused), `INT`, `FLOAT`, `BOOLEAN`, `DATETIME`, `DATE`, `UUID`, `PASSWORD` (hashed, write-only), `JSON`, `ENUM`, `RELATION` (single or many), `COMPONENT` (reusable field groups, single or repeatable) and `DYNAMIC_ZONE` (a list mixing components). This website's pages are built with dynamic zones.

sections.title: See it on your machine
sections.body: The quick start takes a few minutes, with Docker or without.

features.title: Run it with AI
features.summary: A built-in MCP server lets Claude, Cursor and any MCP client read your models and create, edit and publish content in plain language, with the same permissions as the API.

features.title: Models at runtime
features.summary: Create content types in the admin or through the API, in production. The GraphQL schema is regenerated on the fly: no rebuild, no redeploy.

features.title: GraphQL-first
features.summary: Typed queries, filters, sorting, pagination, relations and mutations generated for every model, with a GraphiQL IDE built in.

features.title: Your database
features.summary: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, DynamoDB or embedded RocksDB. Every backend passes the same conformance suite.

features.title: Review workflows
features.summary: Draft and publish for every entry, plus an optional submit → approve workflow per content type, in every edition.

features.title: Roles and scoped tokens
features.summary: Owner, Admin, Contributor, Reviewer and Member roles, limited to some content types if needed, and scoped API tokens for machines.

features.title: Sandboxed plugins
features.summary: WebAssembly plugins installed by admins at runtime, written in Rust, Go, JavaScript and more, with timeouts and memory limits.

features.title: Serverless or container
features.summary: One binary runs as an HTTP server (Docker, VM, Kubernetes) or as an AWS Lambda function.

features.title: Media library
features.summary: Uploads to S3-compatible stores (Garage, MinIO, AWS S3, Cloudflare R2) or the local filesystem, with direct presigned uploads.

features.title: Full-text search
features.summary: Typesense indexing kept in sync with your content, behind a pluggable search engine interface.

features.title: Private by design
features.summary: Opaque, expiring, encrypted ids in the API: database ids never leave the server.

features.title: Portable models
features.summary: tess-transfer exports content models and users to YAML or JSON, to version them or copy them between instances.

competitors.name: Strapi
competitors.summary: The most popular open-source headless CMS, built on Node.js, with a REST API and a GraphQL plugin.

competitors.name: Hygraph
competitors.summary: A hosted, GraphQL-native CMS (formerly GraphCMS), known for content federation across remote APIs.

competitors.name: WordPress
competitors.summary: The world's most used CMS, a PHP application with themes, plugins and a REST API, often used headless through WPGraphQL.

competitors.name: Contentful
competitors.summary: An enterprise headless CMS delivered as SaaS, with REST and GraphQL delivery APIs and a large app ecosystem.

competitors.name: Directus
competitors.summary: A Node.js platform that turns an existing SQL database into REST and GraphQL APIs with an admin app.

competitors.name: Payload
competitors.summary: An open-source TypeScript CMS configured in code, which installs inside a Next.js application.

competitors.name: Sanity
competitors.kind: Hosted content platform with an open-source studio
competitors.summary: A hosted Content Lake with a customizable, open-source React editing studio and its own query language, GROQ.
